title: Machine-readable measurement-and-verification agent skills
description: The four machine-readable 'agent skills' that are the central artifact of the paper 'Encoding measurement-and-verification discipline as machine-readable skills so an AI agent enforces it' (R. Elmér, preprint, 2026). Each skill is a short structured document an AI analysis agent loads automatically when a task matches its triggering description, encoding the mechanical half of a building-energy research programme's measurement-and-verification (M&V) discipline so the agent enforces it by construction: gold-standard (operational/dev standard), research-standard (epistemic ranking, non-circularity, corrections, honest limits), invariant8-mask (a data loader flagging experiment-contaminated and frozen-logger rows), and dhw-cycle-analysis (domain signal-semantics pitfalls). Version 1.2.0 adds the preprint itself (paper/paper9b_preprint.pdf; counts re-measured as of 22 October 2026) and updates the skill documents to the state of 12 October 2026 behind the paper's line counts (gold-standard 199 to 212 lines: a section on the defect classes code reviews keep finding); the other three skills are unchanged from version 1.1.0. Methodology documents only; the controller source code and all personal/household data are excluded. CC-BY-4.0.
notes: The preprint is included in this deposit from version 1.2.0. Canonical skill sources: docs/skills/<name>/SKILL.md in the project repository.
